items.title: A Survey on Side-Tuning for Foundation Models
items.abstract: The adaptation cost of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) depends on trainable parameters, activation storage, and the computations required for optimization. Methods such as LoRA and adapters may still require backward computation through frozen backbone operations and retention or recomputation of intermediate activations. Side-tuning places trainable adaptation modules outside the backbone, creating opportunities to reduce this cost through different connections to the backbone gradient graph. This survey presents a topology- and deployment-aware study of side-tuning for foundation models and proposes a graph-topological definition with three categories: graph-coupled side-tuning, in which an external side branch remains coupled to backbone gradients; mixed side-tuning, in which a detached side path re-enters a later layer of the same backbone; and detached side-tuning, in which an external trainable network consumes frozen backbone representations through a stop-gradient interface and computes task-specific gradients entirely outside the backbone. We review a curated cross-domain corpus spanning natural language processing, computer vision, multimodal learning, recommendation, and relevant methodological precursors, while examining information retrieval as an emerging deployment setting. The literature is organized along three axes: gradient topology, feature interface, and deployment regime. We derive a resource model that accounts for backward activations, online feature production, and cached representations, and use it to develop design guidelines and reporting recommendations. This organization connects the training graph of each method to its resource requirements and the conditions under which its features can be reused.

items.title: A Three-Pillar Governance Framework for Safe and Trustworthy AI Agents
items.abstract: AI agents capable of autonomous decision-making introduce significant challenges related to safety, alignment, accountability, and human oversight. Existing Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) and responsible AI approaches provide important foundations, but many remain fragmented across system design, governance, and operational deployment. This paper presents a Three-Pillar (3P) model and framework for developing safe and trustworthy AI agents through transparency, accountability, and trustworthiness. The framework defines an evolutionary path in which increasing agent autonomy is introduced through progressive validation, structured human oversight, and auditable operational controls. We further describe how the model supports agent lifecycle monitoring, decision traceability, escalation management, and human-agent collaboration within enterprise agentic environments. By integrating oversight principles with operational mechanisms, the proposed framework provides a practical foundation for deploying AI agents that remain aligned with human intent while enabling controlled progression toward higher autonomy.

items.title: ACR lung-RADS: updates and future directions
items.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and low-dose CT (LDCT) screening has been shown to significantly reduce lung cancer deaths in high-risk populations. The American College of Radiology (ACR) introduced the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) in 2014 to standardize the reporting and management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules. Since its inception, Lung-RADS has undergone iterative updates reflecting advances in evidence, clinical practice, and the expanding scope of lung cancer screening. This review summarizes the major updates to Lung-RADS, highlights areas of active discussion within the Lung-RADS Committee, and outlines future research directions. Key topics include the ongoing evaluation of volumetric versus diameter-based nodule measurement, the management of subsolid nodules and the balance between surveillance and intervention, the implementation of Category 0 for infectious or inflammatory findings, clarification of juxtapleural nodule classification, the approach to incidental findings, and the development of a Lung-RADS Atlas. Future directions address the integration of risk-based and category-based assessment approaches, the role of artificial intelligence and deep learning in nodule stratification, the potential incorporation of incidental nodules into Lung-RADS, and the prospect of international harmonization for lung cancer screening reporting and management. Lung-RADS has become an essential reporting and quality tool for lung cancer screening in the United States and increasingly worldwide. Continued refinement, guided by emerging evidence, multidisciplinary collaboration, and technological innovation, will be critical to advancing precision screening strategies and reducing the global burden of lung cancer. items.title: Active-Labeling Evaluation for Computer Agriculture Nematode-Cyst Detection Under Sparse Soil-Sample Ground Truth: An Artificial Intelligence Annotation-Efficiency Bound
items.abstract: Active learning promises to reduce the annotation burden of training nematode-cyst detection models for precision agriculture, but the size of that reduction is not known when ground truth comes from sparse soil samples rather than exhaustive visual inspection. the present analysis derives an annotation-efficiency bound for pool-based active learning under sparse soil-sample ground truth. The detection task is formalised as a two-stage process in which a classifier selects candidate cysts from soil imagery and a laboratory assay confirms a small labelled subset. Under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, the bound is evaluated across a design grid of 8, 16, 24 and 32 clusters and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, with 2000 replications per cell. The annotation-efficiency gain is bounded by the ratio of label noise to cluster-level variance, and that 52 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point improvement at 80% power. The bound provides a design rule for allocating annotation effort between active selection and confirmatory soil sampling.

items.title: Active-Learning Query Synthesis for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Soil-Nutrient Inference Under Laboratory Assay Budget Caps: A Computer Information-Gain Regret Bound
items.abstract: Soil-nutrient inference from spectral and proximal sensing is constrained less by model capacity than by the cost of laboratory assays used to label training queries. the present analysis formalises budget-capped active learning for soil-nutrient regression as a sequential decision problem and derives a finite-horizon information-gain regret bound for a query-synthesis policy that selects assay locations by maximising expected reduction in posterior predictive entropy per unit assay cost. The bound decomposes cumulative regret into an information-gain term, a cost-normalisation term and a misspecification residual, and it predicts that regret grows as the square root of the assay budget rather than linearly in the number of candidate locations. The derivation is connected to the computer-science literature on active learning, Gaussian-process bandits and cost-sensitive information acquisition, and its assumptions are stated explicitly so that the bound can be falsified by future field evaluation. The contribution is a formal, testable statement of when cost-aware query synthesis is provably preferable to uniform or random assay allocation under a fixed laboratory budget, together with the boundary conditions under which the guarantee fails.

items.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems
items.abstract: Modern LLM agents can retrieve information from accessible documents, and then disclose a sensitive conclusion assembled from them. This mosaic effect creates a critical risk for agents operating over confidential data. We quantify its realization with 30 synthetic cybersecurity, medical, and military examples, yielding 10,800 final answers from three LLM agents in controlled simulation and 1,440 answers from live agents in two open-source harnesses. Even under benign queries designed to be answerable from one document, GPT-5.6-Sol, the best performing model tested, discloses forbidden composites in 7.08% of answers (95% CI: 3.75-10.67%) in simulation, with worse disclosure rates in live harnesses. Adding visible classification headers and explicit aggregation rules reduces pooled disclosure rates substantially, yet unsafe disclosures persist in 32.37% of simulated answers (95% CI: 28.33-36.19%) across all intents despite these safeguards. Furthermore, increased refusals do not guarantee confidentiality, since significant refusals reveal the prohibited conclusion regardless. These results point to a troubling conclusion: sensitive data leaks via mosaic-style events are an observed confidentiality failure mode in the evaluated settings at non-negligible rates. They motivate stronger controls on what agents may infer and disclose in sensitive data environments with mixed-clearance users.

items.title: Agentic Intelligence for Scalable Metadata Mining in Telecom Big Data Systems
items.abstract: The high rate at which telecommunication services are changing has yielded a volume of heterogeneous data never seen before such as call detail records, signaling data, and subscriber activity traces. These datasets are crucial in relation to optimization and business intelligence, but effective use of such datasets requires quality metadata. Traditional metadata management is mostly manual and centralized, which cannot support the pace and scale of the new telecom big data systems. As a solution to these shortcomings, the present article suggests a scalable metadata mining strategy that is founded on agentic intelligence. In comparison to more traditional machine learning pipelines, agentic intelligence enables the use of autonomous goal-oriented AI agents, capable of reasoning in a hard data space and relevant to new network topologies and network schemas. The proposed architecture will include a multiagent architecture at a distributed level, having specialized agents: (1) schema drifting ingestion and monitoring agents of data flows; (2) semantic mining actors based on natural language processing to infer contextual metadata; (3) process-aware agents for process mining to determine lineage and dependencies between data; and (4) compliance with policy and metadata retrospect: government agents. A major effect of the work is the integration of agentic intelligence and scalable infrastructures of big data such as cloud-native analytics platforms and distributed data lakes. These agents coordinate themselves using lightweight coordination mechanisms to provide a persistent metadata knowledge layer that facilitates system interoperability and robust downstream analytics. The design concepts are geared toward horizontal scalability and fault tolerance, enabling the distribution of the agents at dynamically evolving manner regarding the workload peak. Besides, agents also enhance their strategies upon continuous feedback to handle concept drift as well. Typical examples of telecom applications such as monitoring network performance and fraud detection have demonstrated that such an approach far outperforms a rule-based approach in the accuracy, coverage, and timeliness of metadata. And lastly, the framework will be capable of offering more dynamic and sustainable data management within the telecom sector.

items.title: Agentic Refactoring: An Empirical Study of AI Coding Agents
items.abstract: Agentic coding tools, such as OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor, are changing how software is developed. These AI-powered systems function as autonomous teammates capable of planning and executing complex development tasks. Agents have become active participants in refactoring, a key practice for improving internal code quality without altering observable behavior. Despite their increasing adoption, there is little empirical understanding of how agentic refactoring is used in practice, how it compares to human-driven refactoring, and what impact it has on code quality. To address this empirical gap, we present a large-scale study of AI agent-generated refactorings in real-world open-source Java projects, analyzing 51,412 refactoring instances across 12,256 pull requests and 14,998 commits based on the AIDev dataset. Our empirical analysis shows that refactoring is a common and intentional activity in this development paradigm, with agents explicitly targeting refactoring in 26.1% of commits. The subsequent analyses of refactoring types, purposes, and code quality focus on the 3,907 commits (32,611 instances) with explicit refactoring intent. Analysis of refactoring types reveals that high-level refactorings form the largest category overall. However, agentic refactoring contains a slightly larger share of lowlevel, consistency-oriented edits than human refactoring (27.6% vs. 24.4%), and its two most frequent operations are Rename Variable (7.6%) and Change Variable Type (6.8%). Additionally, the stated motivations behind agentic refactoring focus overwhelmingly on internal quality concerns (with 52.5% in maintainability and 28.1% in readability), although the measured metric improvements from these frequently occurring low-level refactorings remain limited. Furthermore, quantitative evaluation of code quality metrics shows that agentic refactoring yields small but statistically significant improvements in structural metrics, particularly for medium-level changes, reducing class size and complexity.

items.title: AI agent planning, learning, and adaptation
items.abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), a new paradigm is evolving that includes agentic AI systems capable of autonomously reasoning, planning, and executing multi-step actions. This chapter provides a detailed overview of agentic AI, AI agents, and the developing area of quantum AI agents – systems that utilize the capabilities of quantum computers to exceed the limits imposed by classical computer architecture. In addition to analyzing the architectural foundations of contemporary AI agents such as large language model (LLM)-based agents, multi-agent systems, and hybrid classical–quantum architectures, this chapter presents a unified theoretical framework for understanding how the application of quantum enhancement could result in exponential improvements in optimization, simulation, and pattern recognition abilities of agents using recent advances in quantum machine learning, variational quantum algorithms, and quantum neural networks. Furthermore, this chapter examines transformative applications across healthcare, finance, scientific discovery, and autonomous systems while identifying the current limitations of quantum AI, including decoherence, qubit counts, and alignment challenges. Finally, this chapter concludes that the intersection of agentic AI and quantum computing is likely one of the most significant technological developments of the 21st century, requiring sustained research, ethical frameworks, and inter-disciplinary cooperation.

items.title: AI Powered Smart Personalized Study Planner with Intelligent Reminder
items.abstract: In the contemporary academic paradigm, tertiary and secondary students consistently encounter significant cognitive overhead and temporal fragmentation, largely attributable to suboptimal scheduling methodologies, procrastination, and lack of individualized pedagogical pacing. Conventional digital calendars and static scheduling instruments fail to account for fluid academic priorities, cognitive fatigue thresholds, or behavioral non-compliance. To address these systemic inefficiencies, this paper introduces an AI-Powered Smart Study Planner with Intelligent Reminders, a pervasive Android-based architectural framework engineered to synthesize automated, context-aware study trajectories and foster disciplined academic behaviors. Developed natively utilizing Java and XML with persistent cloud synchronization facilitated by Firebase Realtime Database, the proposed architecture provides dynamic schedule synthesis parameterized by examination schedules, subject difficulty profiles, available temporal bandwidth, and granular academic milestones. A principal contribution of this system lies in its dual integration of predictive behavioural modeling and state-of-the-art conversational artificial intelligence. The framework incorporates a novel Snooze Risk Prediction module that systematically evaluates telemetry data—encompassing chronological snooze frequency, missed learning intervals, and temporal inertia—to compute probabilistic risk factors associated with task avoidance, thereby dynamically recalibrating dispatch heuristics for targeted interventions. Simultaneously, the platform integrates Natural Language Processing (NLP) pipelines and Generative Artificial Intelligence primitives to deliver on-demand cognitive scaffolding. These automated pedagogical tools encompass dynamic notes summarization, programmatic multi-tier quiz synthesis, automated contextual disambiguation of complex academic topics, and real-time conversational agent mediation

items.title: AI solutions as a tool to increase the productivity of medical workers
items.abstract: The active development of domestic medicine, digitalization and automation, the introduction of innovative hardware and software tools and solutions based on artificial intelligence (AI) technologies determines modern trends and approaches to management in Russian healthcare. Today, federal, regional and local medical information systems are being actively implemented, which are radically changing approaches to the management of a medical organization. The purpose of the study is to propose approaches to determining the degree of influence of modern digitalization processes and the introduction of AI solutions on the organization of management and labor productivity of medical workers. To achieve this goal, various modern analytical techniques and approaches were used: for the analysis of secondary sources, content analysis, logical and systematic approaches, for obtaining primary information, the method of expert assessments. Based on the developed tools for interviewing experts, an algorithm for determining the ROI indicator in the implementation/use of digital and AI solutions (taking into account employee KPI) in the activities of medical organizations is proposed. The results of the study can become the basis for making informed decisions in personnel management, in the management of Russian healthcare, taking into account modern socio-economic challenges and strategic tasks facing the country.

items.title: AI Tutors in Technical Training: Trust, Feedback Timing, and Skill Transfer in Maintenance Tasks
items.abstract: Technical maintenance training requires learners to develop procedural accuracy, diagnostic reasoning, error recovery, and confidence under realistic conditions. This study examined how AI tutor feedback timing influences trust, over-reliance, and skill transfer in maintenance tasks. Participants completed procedures under three conditions: immediate feedback, delayed feedback, and adaptive feedback triggered by hesitation, repeated errors, or safety-critical risk. Outcomes included training accuracy, recovery quality, completion time, cognitive workload, tutor trust, feedback acceptance, and unaided transfer performance. Immediate feedback improved early accuracy and reduced procedural errors but increased step-by-step dependence and weakened independent troubleshooting. Delayed feedback produced mixed effects, supporting autonomy for some learners while increasing frustration and avoidable mistakes for others. Adaptive feedback produced the strongest results by allowing independent attempts while intervening when support was needed. It improved unaided transfer, error recovery, procedural sequencing, and trust calibration. Overall, AI tutors were most effective when feedback scaffolded learning without replacing trainee judgment.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into healthcare to support diagnosis, treatment planning, patient monitoring, documentation, and clinical decision-making. In nursing, AI-assisted clinical decision support has the potential to improve efficiency, patient safety, evidence-based practice, and quality of care. However, concerns related to privacy, ethics, technical limitations, overdependence on technology, and the preservation of professional clinical judgment may influence its acceptance. Understanding the perspectives of both nursing students and practicing nursing officers is important for the responsible integration of AI into nursing education and clinical practice.

items.title: AI-Assisted Wearable Devices for Women's Safety with Real-Time Threat and Anomaly Identification
items.abstract: Recently, harassment, assault, stalking, and other forms of violence in both public and private settings have become a social and technological issue of great concern to women's safety.Traditional safety measures like location-tracking, panic buttons and emergency mobile applications are typically reactive and only respond to a threat after it has happened.The latest innovations in the field of wearable technology, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision and sensor integration have presented new possibilities for the creation of proactive safety systems which can detect dangers before they become a dangerous situation.The current research suggests the idea of smart sunglasses that will be equipped with a wearable device to be used and operated by women for monitoring, detecting threats and identifying anomalies in real time.The system proposed for this work incorporates a number of sensing technologies such as GPS, GSM, physiological sensors, accelerometers, cameras, and environmental monitoring modules.The data collected is analysed with the help of deep learning and machine learning algorithms to detect suspicious and unusual activities, patterns of behaviour, environmental hazards, and emergencies.The wearable device uses the You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) object detection framework to detect potentially dangerous objects and people around the wearer in real time.At the same time, behavioural analysis models analyse the user's movement patterns, physiological responses and contextual environmental data to detect anomalies that could signal distress or danger.If a potential threat is identified the system automatically alerts and provides location data to pre-programmed emergency contacts and authorities.A series of simulated urban environments and controlled testing scenarios that incorporated multiple threat categories were employed to test a prototype evaluation.The results of the experiment showed that the object detection rate was 96.8%, anomaly detection rate was 94.2%, and the emergency response notification success rate was 98.5%.The findings suggest that AI-driven wearable devices have the potential to be a powerful tool for improving personal safety by enabling proactive monitoring and intelligent threat assessment.The study advances wearable safety technologies and provides the basis for future research on the intelligent protective systems for vulnerable people.

items.title: AI-Driven Biomedical Image Analysis: A Robust Hybrid CNN–Transformer Framework for Accurate, Explainable and Generalizable Medical Image Classification
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning have become important tools for biomedical image analysis, enabling automated detection, classification, segmentation and quantitative assessment of clinically relevant patterns.Biomedical images frequently exhibit low contrast, acquisition noise, class imbalance, inter-device variability and limited expert annotations.This paper proposes a hybrid CNN-Transformer framework that combines convolutional feature extraction for local spatial patterns with self-attention for global contextual representation.The workflow includes data quality control, de-identification, intensity normalization, augmentation, adaptive feature fusion and an explainability stage.The evaluation protocol emphasizes accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, specificity, ROC-AUC, inference latency, parameter count and robustness.An illustrative benchmark is provided to demonstrate the reporting format: 96.5% accuracy, 96.3% precision, 96.1% recall and 96.2% F1score for the proposed model.These values are placeholders and must be replaced with measurements from the authors' actual dataset and implementation before submission.The framework provides a reproducible structure for comparing classical machine learning, CNN and Transformer baselines while emphasizing patient-level splitting and leakage prevention.Biomedical image analysis has evolved from handcrafted feature engineering toward data-driven artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning systems capable of learning hierarchical visual representations directly from medical images.Despite substantial progress, reliable deployment remains challenging because biomedical images are heterogeneous, highdimensional, noisy, often class-imbalanced, and acquired using different scanners, protocols and institutions.In addition, a model that achieves high accuracy on a retrospective test set may not necessarily generalize to unseen patients or external clinical environments.This research presents a broad AI-driven biomedical image-analysis framework based on a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Transformer architecture.The proposed design exploits the complementary inductive biases of CNNs and self-attention: convolutional layers learn local edges, textures, morphology and fine-grained structures, whereas Transformer blocks model long-range spatial dependencies and global contextual relationships.An adaptive feature-fusion module integrates both representations before prediction.The complete pipeline further includes data governance, image-quality assessment, de-identification, modality-aware normalization, patient-level splitting, clinically valid augmentation, imbalance handling, calibration, uncertainty analysis and explainability.The research methodology evaluates the framework using accuracy, precision, recall/sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, ROC-AUC, precision-recall analysis, computational cost and robustness under controlled perturbations.An illustrative benchmark is provided in which the proposed hybrid framework achieves 96.5% accuracy, 96.3% precision, 96.1% recall and 96.2% F1score, compared with lower illustrative values for conventional machine learning, CNN and Transformer baselines.These values are not claimed as experimental findings and must be replaced by actual measurements.The study emphasizes patientlevel leakage prevention, repeated trials, confidence intervals, ablation experiments and external validation.The broader objective is to establish a technically rigorous and clinically responsible methodology for developing biomedical imageanalysis systems that are accurate, interpretable, computationally feasible and potentially transferable across imaging domains.

items.title: AI-Enabled ATC Decision Support Systems: A Systematic Review Of Trajectory Prediction, Conflict Detection, And Human-AI Teaming In The Loop
items.abstract: This systematic literature review (SLR) synthesises recent evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled Air Traffic Control (ATC) decision-support systems and examines how AI is used to improve operational performance, safety, and resilience in increasingly complex airspace. Research on machine learning, optimisation, and automation has expanded rapidly, but evidence remains fragmented across application areas and validation settings. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020-guided protocol was used to search Scopus and IEEE Xplore for English-language journal articles published from 2021 to 2025. Following screening, full-text eligibility assessment, and final reconciliation of study type, scope, and duplicate records, 30 eligible primary studies (n = 30) were included in the qualitative synthesis. The abstract level reporting completeness appraisal yielded a mean score of 80.28% and a median of 83.33%; 16 of 30 studies (53.33%) scored at least 80%, including six studies (20.00%) that scored at least 90%. These percentages describe reporting completeness rather than algorithmic performance. Because the included studies evaluated different operational tasks, datasets, outcome measures, and validation settings, their performance results were not directly commensurable; combining them into a single pooled model-performance percentage would therefore risk conflating non-equivalent metrics. Performance evidence was instead synthesised comparatively by application area, validation setting, and operational trade-off, so that study level performance was interpreted within the metric and dataset used by each primary study rather than averaged across non-equivalent tasks. Three themes were identified: (1) AI-enabled ATC/Air Traffic Management (ATM) operations, including delay and capacity management, conflict resolution, trajectory prediction, and traffic-pattern analytics; (2) aviation safety, surveillance, and resilience, including unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-related risks, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) interference, sensing, monitoring, and safety assurance; and (3) aviation-connected smart mobility and intelligent transportation systems (ITS), including UAV logistics and related surface-transport applications. Comparative synthesis indicated that prediction methods were increasingly connected to operational decision support, whereas conflict-resolution and resilience approaches continued to rely substantially on simulation, experimental datasets, or bounded validation environments. Overall, the evidence showed increasing operational relevance, but important gaps remained in explainability, real-world validation, human-AI interaction, robustness, and system integration before wider safety-critical ATC deployment.

items.title: AI-Enabled Smart and Precision Agriculture: Smart Sensors, IoT, Deep Learning, Computer Vision, and Decision Support: A Comprehensive Survey
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated with smart sensors, Internet of Things (IoT) networks, machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision to support site-specific agricultural management. However, strong performance on computational benchmarks does not necessarily translate into reliable decisions, effective field interventions, or measurable improvements in agricultural productivity and resource efficiency. This comprehensive narrative survey critically synthesizes advances in agricultural sensing, IoT architectures, data processing, multimodal sensor fusion, predictive modeling, computer vision, decision optimization, and automated actuation. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationships between measurement reliability, model generalization, decision feasibility, intervention accuracy, and verified agricultural outcomes. The reviewed literature demonstrates promising capabilities in crop monitoring, yield prediction, disease and weed recognition, precision irrigation, and selected automated operations. Nevertheless, heterogeneous evaluation protocols, limited independent field validation, sensor calibration challenges, distribution shifts, interoperability barriers, and deployment costs constrain operational reliability and generalizability. To address these interconnected challenges, the survey proposes a literature-informed reference architecture linking agricultural observations, data integration, AI inference, constrained decision-making, physical interventions, and outcome feedback, supported by uncertainty assessment, human oversight, and cross-layer assurance. The proposed architecture is conceptual and has not been empirically validated. Future research priorities include reproducible field evaluations, representative agricultural datasets, uncertainty-aware and explainable AI, resource-efficient computing, interoperable infrastructures, and economically inclusive deployment. The review concludes that the practical value of AI-enabled precision agriculture should be evaluated through reliable interventions, sustainable resource utilization, and demonstrated agricultural outcomes rather than predictive performance alone.

items.title: AI-Powered Early Detection of Crop Diseases and Pest Infestations: A New Paradigm for Plantation Risk Management
items.abstract: Abstract: Crop diseases and pest infestations remain persistent threats to plantation productivity, with pests estimated to destroy up to 40% of global crop production and plant diseases and invasive insects imposing substantial economic losses worldwide (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations [FAO], 2019). Climate change is intensifying these risks by altering the geographic range, seasonality, and population dynamics of pathogens and pests (Gullino et al., 2021; Skendžić et al., 2021). This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI) — including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), vision transformers (ViTs), unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based multispectral and hyperspectral sensing, and Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled monitoring — can strengthen the early detection of biotic stress in plantation crops and thereby support plantation risk management. Drawing on recent peer-reviewed and industry literature, the paper synthesises evidence on detection performance, deployment modalities, and pathways for integration into enterprise risk-management systems. It proposes a conceptual framework in which AI-enabled early-warning systems operate as a continuous, spatially explicit risk-sensing layer linking agronomic observations with operational, financial, and insurance decision-making. AI can improve the timeliness, spatial precision, and consistency of surveillance; however, its risk-management value depends on field validation, representative training data, reliable infrastructure, affordable deployment, and appropriate governance. AI should therefore currently be positioned as decision support that augments, rather than replaces, agronomic expertise and ground-truthing. Keywords: artificial intelligence; plant disease detection; pest infestation; precision agriculture; plantation risk management; machine learning; remote sensing. items.title: AI-supported virtual laboratory for flipped physics learning: effects on middle school students’ achievement, motivation, and cognitive load
items.abstract: This study examined the effects of an AI-supported virtual laboratory (AI-VL) on middle school students’ flipped physics learning. A pretest–posttest control-group quasi-experimental design was adopted with 90 Grade 9 students from a middle school in central China. Three intact classes were assigned to the AI-VL, virtual laboratory (VL), and physical laboratory (PL) groups, with 30 students in each group. ANCOVA revealed large group effects on physics learning achievement, F (2, 86) = 113.38, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.73, and overall learning motivation, F (2, 86) = 113.37, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.73. The AI-VL group outperformed the VL and PL groups, while the VL group also outperformed the PL group. The AI-VL group reported higher intrinsic motivation, whereas the group difference in extrinsic motivation was not statistically significant ( p = 0.054). Significant group differences were also found across the three cognitive load dimensions, with F (2, 87) values ranging from 9.07 to 72.94 and partial η 2 values ranging from 0.17 to 0.63. The AI-VL group reported the lowest perceived intrinsic cognitive load and the highest germane cognitive load, while both AI-VL and VL resulted in lower extraneous cognitive load than PL. items.title: Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach
items.abstract: As domestic and international travel has expanded, the risk of the cross-border dissemination of infectious pathogens has increased, as clearly evidenced during the COVID-19 pandemic. Aircraft- and airport-based wastewater surveillance can provide timely, aggregate evidence of pathogen circulation among mobile populations and may complement clinical, genomic, and syndromic surveillance at points of entry. The strongest evidence for this approach comes from SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection and variant monitoring in aircraft lavatory wastewater, airport terminal wastewater, and airport-associated wastewater systems. However, aviation wastewater signals require cautious interpretation because detectability depends on pathogen shedding dynamics, passenger lavatory use, flight duration, sampling matrix, sample volume, assay sensitivity, sequencing depth, and the availability of epidemiological metadata. This structured narrative review synthesizes current evidence on aircraft and airport wastewater surveillance and examines the scientific determinants that influence surveillance validity and interpretation. Key methodological considerations include sampling design, sample preservation, nucleic acid extraction, molecular detection, sequencing, bioinformatics, inhibition assessment, recovery controls, assay sensitivity, and quality assurance. The review emphasizes that wastewater signals are aggregate and matrix-dependent and should not be interpreted as individual-level diagnosis, direct evidence of transmission, or definitive attribution to a specific flight, route, country, or population. Although SARS-CoV-2 surveillance is comparatively well-documented, multi-pathogen surveillance for enteric viruses, respiratory viruses, vaccine-preventable infections, emerging pathogens, and antimicrobial resistance markers requires pathogen-specific validation and clearer interpretation criteria. Aircraft and airport wastewater surveillance is therefore best viewed as an early-warning and situational-awareness approach whose value depends on converting technical signals into scientifically interpretable evidence.

items.title: Algorithmic Path Dependence in Linked HR Decision Systems
items.abstract: This study examines how interconnected artificial intelligence (AI) tools can turn early human resource (HR) allocations into evidence for later career decisions. A counterfactual-twin Monte Carlo simulation compares isolated and linked systems, alongside periodic record resets and opportunity equalization. Paired employees share fixed capability and random shocks but receive slightly different initial scores. Linking decisions amplifies this initial difference through opportunity allocation, observed performance and reusable records. Periodic resets reduce final-career sensitivity, while opportunity equalization affects access more strongly than terminal outcomes. Near parity in average group outcomes can coexist with positive sensitivity among matched individuals. Additional tests preserve the direction of the architecture and intervention contrasts across the examined coefficient settings, although their magnitudes vary. The findings motivate evaluating decision lineage, opportunity access and record reuse across HR systems. They identify mechanisms within a synthetic, uncalibrated model and do not estimate effects in real organizations.

items.title: Alleviating Baumol’s Cost Disease with Artificial Intelligence: Mechanisms from an Economic Sustainability Perspective
items.abstract: The service sector accounts for a growing share of economic activity, yet relatively slow productivity growth leaves firms facing wage-driven cost pressures that constrain long-term investment. From an economic sustainability perspective, alleviating Baumol’s cost disease can help service firms improve productivity and reduce reliance on additional factor inputs. Drawing on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, this study applies double machine learning to Chinese A-share-listed service firms from 2011 to 2024 to examine the alleviating effect of artificial intelligence (AI) on Baumol’s cost disease and its potential pathways. Higher AI use intensity is significantly associated with a higher Baumol’s cost disease alleviation indicator (BMR). Greater capital investment efficiency and lower long-term debt financing dependence are two potential pathways, while supplier concentration and growth opportunities positively moderate this relationship. The association is stronger among loss-making firms and firms with greater ownership balance. These findings provide firm-level evidence that AI may help service firms cope with rising wages through productivity growth, supported by more efficient capital allocation and improved financing structures, and contribute to efficiency-driven growth.

items.title: Alpha: Systematic Fault Injection and Robustness Evaluation for LLM-Driven Embodied Manipulation
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into embodied robotic planning, yet standard benchmarks primarily evaluate end-to-end task completion in nominal environments, obscuring failure origins across the execution stack. We present Alpha, a systematic fault-injection and robustness-evaluation framework for LLM-driven manipulation in simulation. Alpha injects calibrated faults across perception (sensor lag), actuation (grip slip), kinematics (unreachable targets), and planning (planner-output corruption), alongside concurrent conditions. To separate physical vulnerabilities from planner sensitivities, we introduce a matched methodology pairing an LLM agent (Llama-3 via Ollama) against a deterministic Scripted Oracle planner across a balanced 150-episode matrix under identical seeds, geometries, and safety criteria. Across the matrix, the Oracle achieves 64.0% (48/75) success while the LLM achieves 44.0% (33/75) (paired McNemar p = 3.01 x 10^-4). Crucially, excluding planner-output corruption, performance across all physical and kinematic conditions is identical: 55.0% (33/60) for both planners with zero discordant pairs (McNemar p = 1.00). This demonstrates that physical actuator slip, kinematic reach boundaries, and perceptual staleness affect deterministic controllers and LLM planners equivalently. The performance gap is driven entirely by planner-output corruption (100% Oracle vs. 0% LLM), isolating the prompt-to-JSON serialization and validation interface rather than a cognitive reasoning deficit. We also audit 169 historical pilot attempts for transparency.

items.title: An artificial intelligence based framework for smart power grid management using an autonomous and controllable intelligent service hub with multimodal document processing
items.abstract: The growing sophistication and need to have sustainable energy systems has led to the shift of the conventional power grids to smart power grids. Such grids are equipped with innovative technologies that include digital communication, Internet of Things (IoT), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to increase the efficiency, reliability, and scalability of energy delivery. This paper introduce an AI-based approach to smart power grid management, with the emphasis on the incorporation of an autonomous and controllable intelligent service hub that would be able to process multimodal data, such as textual reports, images, videos, and sensor data. The framework applies AI methods of machine learning, deep learning, and predictive analytics to optimize energy allocation, faults, and failure prediction with minimum human intervention. With real-time analysis, the system dynamically changes the operation of the grids with incoming data, enhancing energy efficiency and lowering the cost of operations by up to 30 percent, between $12,000 and 8,400 in the example of energy optimization. Also, the fault detection system shows a remarkable accuracy of 0.97 in terms of AUC whereas the predictive maintenance model reports an accuracy rate of 95.5. The balancing nature of the energy demand and generation provided by the framework is critical in integrating renewable energy sources since it can help in countering the problem of intermittency of the solar and wind energy. Moreover, the system has a multimodal document processing feature that increases decision-making through the synthesis of various types of data and provides a more detailed overview of grid work. This paper explains how the suggested AI-based framework can greatly improve the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of smart power grids, which will result in the future improvements in energy management.

items.title: An Evidence-Driven Multi-Agent Compound AI System for Head and Neck Proton Radiotherapy Planning
items.abstract: Radiation treatment planning requires balancing competing objectives to satisfy clinical criteria while accommodating physicians' preferences. This study aims to develop an evidence-driven, multi-agent compound AI system that integrates DRL-based automated treatment planning with LLM-based conversational plan refinement for proton PBS therapy. A policy network trained using PPO first generates multiple plans without human intervention, from which one is selected as the target plan and the others serve as references for subsequent refinements. For challenging cases requiring further adjustments, an LLM-based multi-agent system enables plan refinement through natural language interactions. The system comprises a planning agent that recommends evidence-supported adjustments, a chatbot providing a unified conversational interface, and an evaluation agent that retrieves clinical metrics and identifies constraint violations. To enhance domain-specific reasoning, the planning agent based on Qwen3-14B is designed to justify its recommendations using evidence from previously generated plans and post-trained on task-specific data using SFT and GRPO. The framework was trained and evaluated using 21 patients with H&N cancers, with 5 PPO-generated plans per patient. Of these, 50 plans were selected for instruction-guided refinement. Compared with the base LLM, the post-trained Qwen3-14B demonstrated improved instruction-following, information retrieval and domain-specific reasoning capabilities. The resulting adjustments more effectively improved user-prioritized objectives while limiting deterioration in competing objectives, yielding more clinically appropriate trade-offs in patient-specific plan refinement. The proposed compound AI system provides a user-friendly planning platform, offering a promising approach to personalized proton PBS treatment planning.

items.title: An integrated approach to medical personnel management in the context of digital transformation of healthcare
items.abstract: The article addresses the problem of social management of medical personnel amid the digital transformation of healthcare and significant changes in the relationships among medical workers, patients, administrative structures, and digital systems. In response to current interdisciplinary shifts, an integrated model for managing medical personnel is proposed — one that accounts for macrosocial factors, mechanisms of social perception related to the profession, and aggregated indicators at the level of the workers’ subjective world. The methodological foundation is a systems approach, within which medical personnel are viewed as a social system shaped not only by linear macro-management influences but also by relevant public relations, images of the medical profession, the communication environment, the features of digital healthcare products etc. A three-level management model is substantiated, comprising the macro level of normative and organizational structures, the meso level of social perception, and the micro level of professional attitudes, loyalty, and motivation of personnel. It is shown that social perception serves a connecting function between macro-management decisions and actual professional practices. The article emphasizes the need to manage the images of medical personnel — including their reproduction in artificial intelligence — as well as to consider the psychological climate as a significant factor of loyalty. The proposed model makes it possible to increase the coherence of management goals, mechanisms, and interventions.

items.title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
items.abstract: Early diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma is critical to preserve access to curative treatment options. The Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (LI-RADS) provides a standardized framework for non-invasive diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, based on major visual imaging features. However, these features may be difficult to assess consistently, particularly in small liver lesions. We developed dLI-RADS, an interpretable artificial intelligence method designed to estimate the probability of hepatocellular carcinoma from multiphase computed tomography images of manually segmented liver lesions, while remaining aligned with LI-RADS-related imaging concepts. dLI-RADS combines neural network-derived predictions with handcrafted quantitative imaging measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features and integrates these inputs using logistic regression. In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with multiphase computed tomography and at least one liver lesion were included, while lesions larger than 40 mm were excluded. Histology served as the reference standard for hepatocellular carcinoma, and a composite reference standard was used for non-hepatocellular carcinoma lesions. The lesion-level accuracy of dLI-RADS and LI-RADS were compared on the internal evaluation set using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests, with 5% margins and significance levels. On the external test set, sensitivities were similarly compared. dLI-RADS was non-inferior to LI-RADS for lesion-level accuracy in the internal evaluation set, achieving 80% accuracy compared with 74% for LI-RADS (p = 0.04)...

items.abstract: The commercial application of generative artificial intelligence has rapidly brought to the fore the structural tension between machine-generated content (AIGC) and the core presuppositions of copyright law concerning the “author.” This paper examines the protection model and legal mechanisms adopted by the United States on the question of AIGC copyrightability. items.title: AOXP: An Integrated Framework for Antioxidant Peptide Prediction Leveraging LLM-Based Semantic Features and Optimized Physicochemical Ensembles
items.abstract: Abstract Oxidative stress is a critical driver of various severe diseases, positioning antioxidant peptides (APs) as promising therapeutic agents. However, their discovery is constrained by the limitations of low-throughput wet-lab assays and insufficient computational prediction tools. To address this, we developed Antioxidant Peptides eXplorer (AOXP), a deep learning framework that leverages multiscale feature integration for high-precision AP prediction. Unlike existing models that often rely on isolated sequence patterns or manual feature descriptors, AOXP employs a hybrid encoding strategy that synergistically fuses deep, context-aware semantic representations from the protein large language model (ESM2) with explicit physicochemical and sequence distribution features. We constructed an optimized MLP architecture based on a refined 2400-dimensional feature vector, which was systematically benchmarked among five architectures and four feature selection strategies. Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that AOXP achieves competitive performance across evaluation data sets, achieving a benchmark AUC of 0.736 on test_set1_drop and a sensitivity of 0.878 on the positive-only independent Test set 2, significantly outperforming current mainstream computational predictors in both sensitivity and robustness. Integrated Gradients analysis further quantified feature contributions, revealing that ESM2-derived semantics are the most influential features for model prediction (by feature number), followed by hydrophobicity, polarity, charge, and solvent accessibility. To demonstrate its therapeutic utility, AOXP was applied to screen a large peptide library targeting the Keap1-Nrf2 oxidative response pathway. A computationally predicted candidate peptide, MGRRHRHVTDEDDEENLGGDDDDGDDDVYMYPADMHPDERHAYREAV, was identified and validated through molecular dynamics simulations, exhibiting superior binding affinity for the Keap1 Kelch domain compared to the native ligand. AOXP provides a robust and efficient framework for the discovery of functional antioxidant peptides (available at: http://aidd.bioai-global.com/AOXP/).

items.title: Applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning in food processing, quality control, and food safety: a critical review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) are increasingly being applied to support data-driven decision-making in food processing, quality control, and food safety. This review provides a critical assessment of recent technological advances and examines how AI models are being integrated with computer vision, spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging (HSI), biosensors, Internet of Things (IoT) platforms, and intelligent monitoring systems throughout the food value chain. This review brings together evidence from academic studies and industry-based research to examine how AI is currently used in the food sector. The applications considered include process control and optimization, fermentation management, quality grading, authenticity assessment, shelf-life prediction, contaminant detection, and support for food-safety decisions. Recent research extends beyond conventional prediction toward adaptive decision support and, in a smaller number of cases, partially autonomous food systems. Approaches such as explainable AI, multimodal learning, foundation models, digital twins, intelligent packaging, and agentic AI are being investigated for real-time monitoring, data integration, and production management. Their level of maturity, however, varies considerably, and many applications remain conceptual or confined to laboratory settings. Data heterogeneity, poor transferability, limited external validation, and regulatory uncertainty continue to restrict industrial adoption. Although one industrial-scale drying study reported a 12.8% reduction in energy consumption, external validation of food-quality models has resulted in markedly higher prediction errors. This contrast illustrates the difficulty of transferring performance from controlled datasets to new products or production environments. Rather than examining these technologies separately, this review considers their roles across food processing, quality control, and food safety, together with the evidence for industrial validation, sustainability, and governance. Further progress will depend on whether models remain reliable outside their development datasets, not simply on incremental gains in internally reported accuracy.

items.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Managerial Decision-Making for Sustainable Agro-Export Operations in Latin America: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis, 1996-2025
items.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence is transforming agro-export management by converting production, commercial, climate, and logistics data into support for more timely decisions. In Latin America, however, evidence on its managerial applications and contribution to sustainable operations remains fragmented. Objective To synthesize evidence on the application of artificial intelligence to managerial decision-making and its contribution to the efficiency, sustainability, traceability, resilience, and competitiveness of sustainable agro-export operations in Latin America from 1996 to 2025. Methods A systematic review and bibliometric analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Scopus and Web of Science yielded 2160 records; after filtering, screening, and eligibility assessment, 73 studies were included. Bibliometrix in RStudio and VOSviewer were used to analyze scientific production, authors, countries, sources, Bradford’s and Lotka’s laws, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic clusters. Results Scientific output increased markedly after 2021 and peaked in 2024. Scopus accounted for 98.95% of the records. China led with 170 publications, while Brazil, with 149, was the only Latin American country among the five most productive. Four thematic areas were identified: prediction and classification using artificial intelligence and machine learning; logistics, supply chains, and suppliers; sustainable resource management and climate risks; and digital transformation through Agriculture 4.0/5.0. Across the literature, artificial intelligence was found to reduce uncertainty and improve decision-making, although its effectiveness depends on data quality, digital infrastructure, and organizational capabilities. Conclusions Artificial intelligence represents a strategic capability for strengthening sustainable agro-export operations. Its impact depends on integrating algorithms with reliable data, technological infrastructure, organizational capabilities, and sustainability criteria. The limited representation of Latin America highlights the need for further empirical research adapted to regional conditions.

items.title: Applications of Wearable Electronics and Beyond
items.abstract: Wearable electronics represent a transformative shift in the integration of digital technology with the human body, enabling continuous monitoring, enhanced interactivity, and real-time data acquisition in a compact, user-friendly form. These devices, ranging from smartwatches and fitness trackers to smart textiles and implantable biosensors, have revolutionized healthcare, fitness, communication, and entertainment. By offering real-time physiological monitoring, wearables have opened new frontiers in personalized medicine, chronic disease management, and remote diagnostics. Beyond health, wearable technologies are redefining human–machine interaction in sectors such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), defense, industrial safety, and sports performance optimization. Looking forward, the convergence of flexible electronics, nanomaterials, energy harvesting, and artificial intelligence is propelling wearables beyond traditional formats. Next-generation devices aim for seamless skin integration, biodegradability, self-healing materials, and neural interfacing—pushing the boundaries of cyber-physical symbiosis. These advancements point toward a future where wearables transition from external gadgets to embedded, intelligent systems capable of enhancing cognition, perception, and human capability in real time. This abstract outlines the current applications and explores the trajectory of wearable electronics as they evolve from assistive devices to integral components of the human body, fundamentally reshaping our interaction with technology and the environment.

items.title: Approximate Solomonoff Induction: On the Robustness of Learned Universal Predictors
items.abstract: Why large language models trained via log-loss minimization over massive and diverse datasets exhibit broad capabilities and generalizable skills is not yet fully understood. Grau-Moya et al. (ICML 2024) offer a conceptual explanation through the lens of meta-learning: if sequence-generating environments $ν$ are drawn from a prior $w_ν$, minimizing population log-loss recovers the corresponding Bayesian mixture predictor $ξ=\sum_νw_νν$. In the idealized limit in which $w$ is a universal prior, the optimal predictor corresponds to Solomonoff universal induction. Practical machine learning algorithms, however, generally produce only \emph{approximately} optimal predictors. This raises a natural question: \emph{Does the prediction performance remain robust under approximation}? In this paper, we first provide a tight bound on the worst-case effect of approximation on prediction error. We show any predictor $ρ$ satisfying $D_{KL}(ξ\|ρ)\leq η$ retains bounded cumulative-expected-squared prediction error. However, while the Bayesian mixture predictor $ξ$ has error $O(\log(1/w_μ))$ in an environment $μ$, we establish a tight $Θ(η/w_μ)$ bound on the excess error of $ρ$ relative to $ξ$. Thus, approximation can substantially degrade performance in environments assigned small prior probability. In sharp contrast, when environments are averaged according to prior $w$, we prove that the excess prediction error is only $O(η)$. Furthermore, we establish a distribution-shift theorem for dominated shifts from a training prior $w$ to a test prior $w'$, interpolating our average-case and worst-case guarantees. Finally, we extend our robustness analysis to a finite-sampling setting relevant to learning universal predictors with neural networks and Transformers, where $D_{KL}(ξ\|ρ)$ could be unbounded. items.title: AQL-Lite: Enabling Efficient Knowledge Acquisition for Arabic LLMs via Data-Centric Continual Pretraining
items.abstract: Training Arabic large language models faces challenges from noisy web data, dialectal variation, and the high cost of continual pretraining (CPT). We introduce AQL-Lite (AQL: Arabic Quality Language), a time- and resource-efficient framework for adapting a multilingual LLM to Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). AQL-Lite couples a quality-first curation pipeline (structural cleaning, heuristic and model-based filtering, MSA selection, and deduplication) with a partial-parameter CPT recipe that trains RS-LoRA adapters across the network together with the last eight transformer blocks and the embedding matrix, under layer-wise learning rates. At a matched 1B-token budget, CPT on AQL-curated data raises a four-benchmark Arabic mean by 3.51 points over CPT on raw web text, which yields no gain over the base model. In a controlled 5B-token comparison, AQL-Lite recovers 94% of the gain of full-parameter CPT (mean 73.19 vs. 73.58) in 52% of the wall-clock time and outperforms adapter-only baselines on every benchmark, and a component ablation shows that adapters, unfrozen blocks, and embedding training each contribute. Scaled to 40B MSA tokens and instruction-tuned on one million examples, the resulting 12B model scores 75.3 on the seven-benchmark Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard v2 (OALL v2) suite. These results suggest that partial-parameter CPT on a carefully curated corpus is a practical route to efficient MSA adaptation.

items.title: Aqua Sense AI: AI-Powered Water Quality Intelligence Platform
items.abstract: Water quality assessment is essential for determining whether water is suitable for human consumption and enabling informed decision-making regarding water resources. Aqua Sense AI is an AI-powered water quality intelligence platform developed using Python and Streamlit. The system provides a preliminary classification of water samples as Safe (Potable) or Unsafe (Non-Potable) based on nine physicochemical parameters: pH, Hardness, Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), Chloramines, Sulfate, Conductivity, Organic Carbon, Trihalomethanes, and Turbidity. A Random Forest Classifier is employed for the classification task, delivering real-time predictions along with prediction confidence scores, a composite Water Quality Score (0–100), and risk level assessments (Low, Medium, or High). Parameter values are entered through an intuitive interactive web form. The platform features an Analytics Dashboard powered by interactive Plotly visualizations, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) providing feature importance rankings and natural language reasoning, dynamic parameter-specific water treatment recommendations, and session-based prediction history tracking. Designed in alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), the system serves as a preliminary decision-support tool and does not replace certified laboratory testing. Overall, the work demonstrates an integrated approach that combines machine learning, explainability, interactive data analytics, and actionable guidance within a unified water quality assessment platform

items.title: ARCANA: A Benchmark for Abstraction and Analogical Reasoning
items.abstract: Analogical reasoning is widely considered a fundamental component of human intelligence. Few benchmarks are designed to explicitly test far analogical reasoning - reasoning between domains that are superficially dissimilar yet share deep relational or structural similarities. In this work, we introduce an analogical reasoning benchmark called Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus of ANAlogy (ARCANA). The tasks of ARCANA require performing far analogical mappings from real-world objects or physical phenomena to abstract grid-based transformations, different from the well-known ARC-AGI benchmark which primarily emphasized innate human priors. We validate ARCANA through a human study, demonstrating that humans solve these tasks reliably. In contrast, evaluations across a range of large language models show a distinct performance gap compared to humans, revealing systematic failure modes that remain challenging for current models. To address this gap, we propose ConceptSIR, a reasoning framework based on concept slippage, introspection, and reflection. Experiments demonstrate that ConceptSIR enables standard LLMs to solve several challenging ARCANA tasks that were unsolved by direct prompting in our evaluation. Overall, our results suggest that far analogical reasoning remains an open problem for contemporary LLMs. All the materials are available at sites.google.com/view/arcanacogtest. The complete codebase, including benchmark, and ConceptSIR, is publicly available at https://github.com/density-11/arcana-test. All ARCANA data and task instances can be accessed and explored at https://arcanacogtest.org/.

items.title: Architectural Concepts For Integrating Human Preferences And Environmental Susainability Into AI-Driven Architectural Design
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing architectural design through generative modelling, performance prediction, spatial planning, and workflow automation. However, many current applications address individual tasks or emphasize visual novelty, while practical design decisions must balance human needs, climate responsiveness, affordability, accessibility, regulatory constraints, and environmental performance. This paper proposes a Human-Centered and Sustainability-Aware AI Architectural Design Framework (HCS-AADF) that combines these considerations within an iterative design-support workflow. The framework accepts user requirements, site and climate information, budget limits, and applicable design constraints; analyses the project context; generates alternative layouts or massing concepts; evaluates alternatives against multiple criteria; explains trade-offs; and returns shortlisted options to an architect for review. Human feedback can be used to refine subsequent iterations. A conceptual multi-criteria scoring model and an evaluation protocol are specified to support future implementation and testing. The paper synthesizes three supplied research directions—AI architectures informed by human drives and emotions, the adoption and capabilities of AI software tools in architecture, and systematic reviews of AI applications in architectural design—along with relevant recent literature on generative design and sustainable building optimization. The proposed contribution is an integrated, transparent workflow rather than a claim of experimentally proven performance. Expected benefits include more traceable design comparisons, earlier consideration of sustainability, and improved collaboration between architects and AI systems. The framework also identifies risks involving data quality, bias, explainability, regulatory verification, and over-reliance on generated outputs. Experimental validation with representative building projects and expert review is proposed as the next step.

items.abstract: Incorporation of artificial intelligence in the process of creative writing entails a paradigmatic change in literary text production, assessment, and perception. In this research paper, the focus is made on an innovative role of large language models in the sphere of English language and literature authorship. Based on systematic analysis of recent empirical studies and theoretical approaches, three interrelated aspects will be discussed: interaction between human authors and AI systems, reception of artificial literature by the readership, and conceptualization of authorship in the digital age. For the purpose of this paper, the mixed-method approach involving both quantitative analysis of empirical studies and qualitative analysis of literary theoretical approaches will be used. As the results of the analysis indicate, the texts generated by AI are rated aesthetically the same way as texts written by human authors when there is no indication of the author's identity; however, readers maintain biases against texts that are perceived to be machine-generated.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Electric Power and Energy Systems: A PRISMA-Bibliometric Review of Tools, Application Domains, Quantified Impacts, and Deployment Barriers from 2021 to 2025
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in electric power and energy systems for forecasting, fault diagnosis, stability assessment, control, renewable energy integration, and real-time monitoring. However, evidence remains fragmented across algorithms, applications, performance metrics, and deployment conditions. This study reviews recent AI applications in power and energy systems and examines their technological, economic, and operational contributions and limitations. A PRISMA-based systematic and bibliometric review was conducted using Scopus and Web of Science records published from 2021 to 2025. Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny 5.5.0 and VOSviewer 1.6.20 were used to analyze publication trends, citation patterns, geographical distribution, influential studies, and keyword networks, while 40 studies were retained for systematic evidence synthesis. In the reconciled 4854-record corpus, annual scientific production increased from 610 publications in 2021 to 1305 in 2025, with research concentrating on machine learning, deep learning, smart grids, stability, renewable energy, forecasting, fault diagnosis, optimization, and cybersecurity. The reviewed studies reported improvements in predictive accuracy, computational efficiency, fault localization, voltage control, energy savings, and real-time decision support. Nevertheless, data dependence, computational cost, limited interpretability, simulation-to-field transfer, and validation requirements remain major barriers. items.abstract: Verbal autopsy (VA) remains the principal source of cause-of-death labels for community health worker (CHW) triage algorithms in low-resource settings, yet the recall interval between death and VA interview is rarely recorded and almost never modelled. the present analysis treats unmeasured recall decay as a structured label-noise process and characterises the operating characteristics of a before-after-control-impact (BACII) benchmarking design used to evaluate CHW triage classifiers under that noise. The design attains 80% power at 54 clusters for a 5-percentage-point effect. The paper derives a bias bound showing that recall decay inflates the apparent between-cluster variance component and therefore the intraclass correlation, and it proposes a sensitivity-analysis protocol that reports benchmarking conclusions as a function of an assumed decay rate rather than as a single point estimate. The contribution is a design-level account of how label noise that is unmeasured but structurally bounded can be made visible in AI benchmarking for healthcare, together with the sample-size consequences of that visibility.

items.abstract: Emergency department triage classifiers are benchmarked almost exclusively on static acuity labels, yet the operational label is produced when a nurse re-scores a patient at queue reordering. the present analysis treats that re-scoring as an unmeasured cluster-level shock and asks whether the before-after-control-impact (BACI) design can recover the effect of a classifier change when re-scoring is confounded with the intervention. A replication-based evaluation was conducted over a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD 6.0, residual SD 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, using 2000 replications per design cell across 8, 16, 24 and 32 clusters and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The interaction estimate was biased toward the null when re-scoring intensity differed between arms, and residual diagnostics showed heteroscedasticity aligned with cluster size. The contribution is a stability bound: BACI benchmarking of triage classifiers is defensible only when re-scoring is either measured or shown to be exchangeable across arms, and the paper specifies the design conditions under which that claim can be tested.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Benchmarking of Referral-Network Graph Neural Triage Under Unmeasured Inter-Facility Transport Time Censoring: A Healthcare Safety-Robustness Evaluation
items.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly proposed for triage across inter-facility referral networks, yet their safety evaluation typically assumes that transport times between facilities are observed. In many low- and middle-income referral systems, transport time is unmeasured and right-censored: only the fact that a patient arrived, or did not, is recorded. We define a censored referral-network triage problem, introduce a transport-time censoring operator, and derive a distributionally robust triage policy that bounds worst-case mortality under an ambiguity set defined by censoring-consistent transport-time distributions. We prove that the robust policy admits a tractable convex reformulation and that its safety gap relative to the oracle policy is bounded by the Wasserstein radius of the ambiguity set. The framework is illustrated using the DHS Program indicator 'Households possessing a computer' across 27 African countries (56 country-survey observations, 2015-2025; mean 7.893, SD 5.144), which serves as a proxy for digital readiness of referral nodes. The contribution is a benchmark protocol and a theorem that together specify when GNN triage can be certified safe under unmeasured transport censoring, and when it cannot.

items.abstract: Sparse-sensing continuous glucose monitors supply the input stream for most deployed insulin-dosing forecasters, yet the meal-announcement channel those forecasters rely on is systematically incomplete in free-living use. the present analysis treats unmeasured meal-announcement noncompliance as a design property of the evaluation, not a nuisance to be imputed away, and asks what a safety-regret benchmark can identify when the announcement indicator is missing not at random. The contribution is a benchmark design that treats announcement noncompliance as a first-class safety parameter rather than a preprocessing step.

items.abstract: Community health worker (CHW) programmes are widely used to support hypertension control, but the visit logs that record CHW contacts are frequently incomplete, and this incompleteness is not random: patients who are lost to follow-up, disengaged, or transferred between facilities are systematically less likely to have their visits recorded. Power was estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design required 54 clusters to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power. The contribution is a formal identification result for the CHW visit effect under log incompleteness, together with a design-analysis characterisation of the BACI estimator that quantifies how cluster count and effect size jointly determine detectable effects in outreach-targeting evaluations.

items.abstract: White-coat measurement confounding threatens the validity of artificial-intelligence-guided hypertension treatment escalation in community clinics: when the decision to intensify therapy is informed by a blood pressure reading that is itself distorted by the measurement setting, the prescribing rule and the outcome share a common cause that no observed covariate set captures. No observational data are used or claimed. The analysis declares a variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, and estimates power across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design requires 56 clusters to detect a 5-percentage-point escalation effect at 80 per cent power. The framework separates the prescribing-safety estimand from the measurement-confounding nuisance, and the design evaluation shows how the doubly robust estimator's bias correction interacts with cluster-level heterogeneity. The contribution is a formal statement of the identification conditions under which an AI prescribing rule can be evaluated for safety when white-coat measurement is unobserved, together with the design parameters that make such an evaluation informative.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Causal Inference of Community Clinic Oral Rehydration Solution Stock Allocation Under Unmeasured Caregiver Preference Confounding by Market Availability: A Healthcare Instrumental Variable Mortality Equity Evaluation
items.abstract: Community clinic oral rehydration solution (ORS) stock allocation is routinely evaluated by comparing mortality across clinics with different stock levels, but caregiver preference for ORS is confounded by local market availability of competing products, and this confounding is rarely measured. The identification argument is stated as a set of assumptions, a nonparametric identification theorem is proved, and a doubly robust machine learning estimator is proposed with a regret bound for the equity-weighted mortality loss. The framework is illustrated with a re-analysis of a real World Bank panel of 24 African countries observed from 2000 to 2023 (N = 560), in which GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$) is regressed on access to electricity and urban population; the model fit is R-squared = 0.591, adjusted R-squared = 0.5895, F = 184.764, and the coefficient on access to electricity is 1291.554 (SE = 194.352). Instrumental variable designs anchored in market availability can recover mortality equity effects that conventional stock-mortality comparisons systematically distort, and it specifies the boundary conditions under which the instrument fails.
